title: Letter grades
objective: letter_grade(score) should turn a numeric score into a letter grade.
expected: 90 and above is "A", 80-89 is "B", 70-79 is "C", 60-69 is "D" and anything below 60 is "F".
constraints: Boundary scores belong to the higher grade, so 80 is a "B".

advice.diagnosis: The comparisons use >= when they should be strict, so boundary scores are pushed into the wrong grade.
advice.rationale: Switching every >= to > makes each band exclusive at its lower edge, which removes the overlap between grades.
advice.note: Incorrect. The real problem is the order of the checks: score >= 60 is tested first, so every passing score becomes "D". The patch also breaks the boundaries (60 becomes "F").

prediction.question: After applying the suggested patch, what does letter_grade(95) return?

failingTestCheck.question: With the patch applied, the test letter_grade(95) still fails. What does this failing test show?
options: A score of 95 is caught by an earlier condition, so the order of the checks is the problem
The boundary at 95 needs a strict > comparison
The test expects the wrong value
Python cannot compare integers with >= reliably
failingTestCheck.answer: A score of 95 is caught by an earlier condition, so the order of the checks is the problem
